Paragraph: Arjuna saw standing there fathers, grandfathers, teachers, maternal uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons, and companions as well. Seeing all these kinsmen arrayed for battle, filled with deep compassion and uttering this in sadness, Arjuna spoke: 'O Krishna, seeing my own people present here, eager for war, my limbs yield, my mouth dries up, my body trembles, and my hair stands on end. My bow Gandiva slips from my hand, and my skin burns all over. I am unable to stand, and my mind seems to be whirling. I see adverse omens, O Kesava, nor do I see any good in killing my own kinsmen in battle.'
Situation/Problem_Faced: On the threshold of the Kurukshetra war, Arjuna experiences sudden acute panic, ethical paralysis, and overwhelming panic symptoms upon recognizing that victory requires killing his own family members and venerated teachers.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Arjuna expresses his complete loss of resolve and emotional breakdown to Krishna, refusing to fight and surrendering to his inner turmoil while seeking guidance.
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna drops his weapons and collapses in the chariot, setting the stage for Krishna to impart the psychological and philosophical discourse of the Bhagavad Gita to restore his mental clarity.

Moha (Delusion caused by selective attachment to kinsmen)
Karpanya (Pity, weakness of heart, and feeling spiritually/psychologically impoverished)
Dharma-Sammudha-Chetah (Mind bewildered regarding core duty and righteousness)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Arjuna's breakdown represents 'Vishada'—a severe existential crisis where ego-driven attachment (Moha) blinds an individual to universal duty (Dharma). His crisis, though painful, serves as the necessary prelude to receiving higher spiritual wisdom.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: This passage describes a classic panic attack triggered by extreme moral injury and cognitive overload. Arjuna exhibits both somatic symptoms (tremors, dry mouth, burning skin) and cognitive paralysis (whirling mind, loss of motor control), demonstrating how overwhelming relational conflict destroys decision-making capabilities.
